modifications: Renamed from good-readme to oss-readme on migration into oss-kit.
Style guidance removed in favour of citing oss-writing.

Badges reversed. Upstream's Clean up step removes every badge as a drag on readability. This fork keeps at most three, version then CI then coverage, in their own paragraph below the opening sentence, because each shows a live fact that changes without anyone editing the README. Everything else is still cut. references/badges.md is new here: upstream is a single SKILL.md with no references directory, verified at the pinned SHA and on main. That file carries the per-ecosystem URL templates, prefers a provider's documented native badge over a Shields.io proxy, and states the live-fact test that decides what never gets a badge.

Opening block narrowed and section order changed. Upstream asks the first paragraph for three things: what it does in plain language, how the user benefits, and what makes it different from alternatives. R-DOC-01 keeps only what it does, adds who it is for, and caps it at one sentence. The differentiator moved to the edge bullet of the facts list, which R-DOC-10 checks. Upstream then runs opening, facts, example, getting started, putting the example before any install step. R-DOC-02 requires install then example, so the two are merged into one Install and example section.

Worked examples come from this repository rather than from a named third party. Upstream demonstrates its opening block with a well-known project's README. Every such README breaks a rule this standard holds, usually R-DOC-01 or R-DOC-02, so quoting one teaches the departure along with the shape, and a quoted README goes stale the day its project edits it. The numbers in these examples are checked against STANDARD.md by tests/rule-counts.test.ts.

Sections added with no upstream counterpart: where to start for a project with more than one entry point, help and status, links to the license, changelog, and contributing guide, and the rule that every fenced block says what consumes it.

Clean-environment verification, renderer-specific alerts, generated outlines, installation provenance, and image accessibility were aligned with current GitHub, GitLab, Codecov, and upstream package documentation.

The body states the badge cap and points at references/badges.md for everything else, so the cap, the order, the placement, the live-fact test, and the per-ecosystem URL templates have one statement rather than a summary competing with the file. Upstream has no references directory to point at. Clean-environment verification names the run: an empty mktemp -d directory, the lowest supported runtime, the guide's commands pasted in order, and no global change to make a step pass. The forge repository description is read here and edited by oss-community, which R-COM-07 names as its owner; upstream is one skill and draws no such boundary. The skill names three ways in, and one of them reviews without editing: it reports the checklist items that fail, anchored at the line each fails at, and changes no file. Upstream instructs only writing.
